items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: Lunceford had his nose in the air though, he was a school teacher

ctx.x: It seems to me that the players at that time were not only good players, but real personalities.

Yeah, you know you had to, had to be nice too, you know because if you didn’t, you didn’t get the gig, you know? You had to do more than just play. You had to be a nice person, because we had a lot of friends, you know, and that’s what they wanted you to have. They used to say, well Basie was just a, Basie was just a cat, a down to earth cat. There was much difference between he and Duke. Duke was a beautiful cat, but he associated with bigger people, you know, like doctors and things like that. You might catch…
and he wanted the band to be just students, I mean school kids like. There was a lot of different personalities and things.

items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: I would put it like the Jimmy Lunceford style.

ctx.x: Had a nice arrangement on that. "The First Time I Saw You." You know, I'll tell you though, I think Nat T'oles' band was closer to -- I would put it like the Jimmy Lunceford style.
